channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=75) found that high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises (UNGE) yielded superior electrophysiological and functional outcomes compared to extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT)+UNGE or UNGE alone in patients with post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome, with benefits maintained at 12 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy on pain intensity and functional disability in chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs found that extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), particularly radial ESWT (rESWT), significantly reduced pain in chronic low back pain (SMD = -0.72; 95% CI -1.30 to -0.14), but functional disability improvements (MD = -6.12) did not reach the minimal clinically important difference.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical activity guidelines' impact on cognition in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (n=462) found that meeting physical activity guidelines for multiple sclerosis (PAG-MS) significantly improved processing speed (SMD = 0.29), visuospatial memory (SMD = 0.47), and verbal memory (SMD = 0.75) in individuals with MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 45 chronic low back pain patients found that treadmill exercise with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE) led to greater improvements in Timed Up and Go performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and trunk repositioning errors compared to treadmill exercise alone or core stabilization exercises.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study of 92 older adults with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears found that 95-97% of patients achieved minimal clinically important difference at 3 months, with 100% achieving it by 4 years with nonoperative treatment. Longer symptom duration and smoking were associated with worse shoulder function, while diabetes was linked to higher pain intensity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A three-arm randomized controlled trial of 60 chronic stroke patients found that both Sensory Electrical Stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG), combined with conventional physical therapy, produced greater improvements in Action Research Arm Test scores (adjusted mean gains of 12.05 and 12.44 points, respectively, both P < .001) compared to conventional physical therapy alone, with no significant difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of short-foot and toe-curl exercises on movement control during single-leg landing after ACL reconstruction: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
item.description: In ACLR patients, short-foot exercise (SFE) significantly reduced hip adduction excursion during single-leg landing compared to toe-curl exercise (TCE) at 6 weeks (between-group difference -6.30°, ES -1.41) and 12 weeks, suggesting SFE facilitates earlier improvement in frontal-plane movement control.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: Adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) provided negligible additional improvements in pain intensity (MD -0.4 points), disability (MD -0.7 points), or circulating PGE2 concentrations compared with sham PBMT plus MCE at 6 weeks and throughout 12-month follow-up in 148 adults with chronic non-specific low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of functional inspiratory muscle training on diaphragm function and core stabilisation in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=40) found that a 10-week multicomponent functional inspiratory muscle training (F-IMT) program significantly improved diaphragm thickness (adjusted difference, 2.434 mm; 95% CI, 1.714 to 3.261; P < .001) and mobility, reduced pain, and increased respiratory muscle strength and core endurance in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain, compared to thoracic expansion exercises.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (N=1177) found chronic physical exercise training improved the metabolic cost of walking (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) in healthy adults (g = 0.49, p = 0.001), but not significantly in stroke patients (g = 0.24, p = 0.065).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Modality-specific, deficit-targeted exercise prescriptions for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 61 RCTs (N=3706) found multicomponent training with resistance training provided the most comprehensive benefits for functional mobility, while elastic band resistance training was most effective for handgrip strength (MD = 1.95 kg, 95% CI: 1.13 to 2.76) with moderate certainty.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Construct validity and intrasession intra-rater reliability of the stair and step tests in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
item.description: In 100 MS patients, both the Stair Test (ICC 0.997) and Step Test (ICC 0.955) showed excellent test-retest reliability and strong construct validity with other mobility scales. These tests offer a practical, fast, and low-fatigue solution for monitoring mobility in MS.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapists' perspectives on direct access in a referral-based system in Austria - A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study of 10 Austrian physiotherapists found perceived readiness for direct access but identified gaps in confidence for red-flag screening and challenges with legal uncertainty and hierarchical physician relationships.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Barriers and Facilitators Influencing Physiotherapists' Adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines and Return to Sport Criteria after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Qualitative Study in Austria.
item.description: A qualitative study in Austria explored barriers and facilitators for physiotherapists' adherence to ACLR CPGs and RTS criteria. Nine physiotherapists participated, revealing limited guideline usability, patient expectations, professional attitudes, and interprofessional misalignment as key barriers, while structured guidelines and professional development facilitated adherence.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility of Distributed Wearable Ultrasound for Detecting Neuromuscular Coordination Differences After Knee Injury
item.description: A feasibility study with 20 NCAA Division I women athletes (8 with prior knee injury) using a four-channel distributed wearable ultrasound (D-WUS) system revealed significant differences in right-limb VL-VMO correlation (p = 0.029) and timing symmetry (p = 0.019) in injured participants during countermovement jumps, despite similar jump performance metrics.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Do treatment parameters of dry needling influence its effect on pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 71 comparisons, with 23 in quantitative synthesis, found no consistent evidence that dry needling treatment parameters (number of sessions, muscles treated, or local twitch responses) moderate its effectiveness for neck pain, citing high heterogeneity and incomplete reporting.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Trends in Australia's physiotherapy workforce: changes and future implications.
item.description: Analysis of Australia's National Health Workforce Dataset (2013-2023) showed a 70.5% increase in physiotherapists (from 21,046 to 35,889), but 81.0% still practiced in metropolitan areas. Males were 15% less likely than females to practice in regional centers, while Indigenous physiotherapists were 85% more likely to practice outside metropolitan areas.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of bimodal signal biofeedback on the supraglottic swallowing maneuver in patients with post-stroke dysphagia: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 post-stroke dysphagia patients found that adding bimodal biofeedback (accelerometer and nasal airflow sensor) to supraglottic swallowing maneuver training significantly improved Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) scores (p < 0.001) and reduced the percentage of Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS) scores ≥ 6 (p = 0.026) after 2 weeks and at 1-month follow-up, compared to conventional therapy alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A multimodal non-fatiguing recovery strategy improves neuromuscular restoration and attenuates inflammatory and oxidative stress responses following a standardized football match: a randomized crossover study
item.description: A randomized crossover study in 20 male semi-professional football players found a multimodal non-fatiguing recovery strategy (low-intensity cycling, foam rolling, percussive therapy) showed smaller post-recovery declines in peak force (−7.5% vs −14.3% in passive recovery) and other neuromuscular outcomes, along with smaller increases in muscle damage and inflammatory markers.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Impact of malnutrition and protein-enriched oral nutrition on early recovery after fragility fractures in older adults: the NuTra trial
item.description: A single-center RCT (N=218) found that a protein-enriched diet during acute hospital stay did not significantly improve in-hospital medical complications, surgical site infections, or functional mobility at discharge in older adults with fragility fractures at nutritional risk.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics
